context.body: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: David seeks a survivor of Saul’s house for Jonathan’s sake, restores Saul’s land to Mephibosheth, seats him at the royal table, and appoints Ziba’s household to work the land.
observations.label: Power remembers Jonathan’s covenant: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Mephibosheth, Ziba, Jonathan, and Saul’s house, the royal table, Lo Debar, and restored land, seeking, summoning, fearing, restoring, eating, appointing, and bowing visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Power remembers Jonathan’s covenant: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, Mephibosheth, Ziba, Jonathan, and Saul’s house · the royal table, Lo Debar, and restored land · seeking, summoning, fearing, restoring, eating, appointing, and bowing · covenant loyalty changes Mephibosheth’s place and provision
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 9:1–13

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 9:1–13 as its own ark, house, and kingdom David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places covenant loyalty changes Mephibosheth’s place and provision inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Power remembers Jonathan’s covenant
